analysis.summary:
How it works (checked in the bytes of Wiz8.exe and sr.dll, and matching the decomp):
1. The game draws all of its 2D into one 640x480 16-bit DirectDraw surface held in system memory (g_primary_surface 0x6596A8). It is created by InitializePrimaryDirectDrawSurface 0x426080 with DDSCL_NORMAL, flags 0x1007, caps 0x840 (OFFSCREENPLAIN|SYSTEMMEMORY), 640x480, 16 bpp. This surface is never shown on screen directly. InitializeRendererSceneObjects 0x423500 wraps its memory in an srColorSurface (type 9 = ARGB1555, pitch taken from Lock), stored in g_primary_color_surface 0x659660. At 0x423D42-0x423D73 it then builds stSurface2D(surface, 640, 480, parent = g_scene_overlay0 [0x659654], tile 128) and stores it in g_surface_node 0x659664.
2. stSurface2D cuts the canvas into 5 columns x 4 rows = 20 textures of 128x128 (stTexture2D, clamp wrap). Each texture pulls its pixels from the shared surface. Object fields confirmed from the code: +0x13C vertex mask, +0x140 shader bits (0x800000 = alpha test), +0x144 tile size, +0x148 columns, +0x14C rows, +0x150 tile count, +0x15C tile array, +0x160 tile_u = 128/640, +0x164 tile_v = 128/480, +0x170 texcoords.
3. Upload: the game writes pixels into the surface and marks 8x8 cells dirty in an 80x60 table (0x652DDC). FlushDirtyTiles 0x425B40 is called from RenderFrame at 0x4268C2, before beginFrame. It merges dirty cells into rectangles and calls stSurface2D::updateRectangle 0x47E450, which sends them through srGERD::setTextureSubImage.
4. Drawing: the canvas is a scene node of g_scene_overlay0. Its only draw path is vtable slot 0x5EC76C -> process 0x47E0F0 -> DrawTiles 0x47E100. There is no direct call anywhere else (references to g_surface_node: 0x423D74, 0x423DD9, 0x425572, 0x425C0E, 0x4297E6 only). DrawTiles does the following:
   - pushes and loads the projection with srGERD::ortho(0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1). I decoded the 12 dword pushes at 0x47E138-0x47E152: left 0, right 1, bottom 1, top 0, near 0, far 1. So y points down and the canvas uses normalized 0..1 coordinates.
   - sets clip state 0x3F, cull none, the shader from node+0x140 and texcoords from node+0x170; antialias off.
   - draws one 4-vertex triangle strip per tile at x = col*0.2 .. (col+1)*0.2 and y = row*0.2667 .. (row+1)*0.2667, z = -0.1. The last row goes past 1.0 (512 > 480) and is clipped.
   - pops the matrix at the end.
   - It **never sets a viewport**. The 0..1 square is stretched over whatever srGERD viewport is current.
5. Viewport in effect: the canvas is drawn by RenderScene 0x427850 (cdecl: scene, camera, const int* vp640, bool preserve_fog).
   - With vp640 == NULL it does not touch the viewport at all.
   - With vp640 != NULL it sets viewport and scissor to vp*W/640, vp*H/480 (unsigned math), renders, then resets both to (0, 0, W, H).
   - W and H come from srGERD::getWidth/getHeight, which read [gerd+0x380] and [gerd+0x384].
   - srGERD::setViewPort (sr.dll 0x1001D410) only stores left/top/right/bottom at gerd+0x1638..0x1644 and sets dirty bit 0x80 in gerd+0x24. Scissor is stored at gerd+0x1628..0x1634.
   - So all 2D drawn with vp NULL fills the full back buffer, and the overlay camera (view plane 0..1) maps 0..1 onto that same viewport.
6. RenderFrame 0x426790 draw order, confirmed from the call sites:
   - setClearColor(fog colour), FlushDirtyTiles, beginFrame.
   - Optional clear of the g_viewport area only (0x42692C-0x426A1D, only when blacked out / no sky world).
   - prerender[active^1] and prerender[active] (overlay camera, vp NULL) at 0x426A3A / 0x426A57.
   - Secondary/sky world with &g_viewport 0x6595E8 at 0x426A9F, then the world scene with &g_viewport at 0x426BC6 or 0x426C0D.
   - Then, if g_overlay_scenes_enabled 0x603C6D:
     - g_scene_fullscreen (vp = g_overlay_viewport 0x659668), only if g_fullscreen_scene_last 0x603C4C == 0;
     - **g_scene_overlay0 (the canvas), vp NULL, at 0x426C68**;
     - g_scene_user, vp NULL, at 0x426C7E;
     - g_scene_square (g_square_camera 0x659674, vp = g_overlay_viewport) at 0x426C99;
     - g_scene_fullscreen at 0x426CC0 if the flag is set;
     - the cursor scene, vp NULL, at 0x426CE3.
   - endFrame.
7. Is the world drawn first and does it show through? Yes, the 3D world is drawn before the canvas. It shows through only where the canvas uses alpha test. stSurface2D::setAlphaTestEnabled 0x47E370 (reached via the wrapper 0x425570, 15 callers) ORs 0x800000 into the shader bits (+0x140) and switches every tile's texture hint between ONE_BIT_ALPHA and NO_ALPHA. Per the decomp, the main game screen turns it on and the menu screens (character, journal, options, automap, party, etc.) turn it off. With it on, ARGB1555 pixels whose top bit is 0 are discarded. Areas cleared to 0 (for example by ClearSurfaceRect 0x4263F0) become holes through which the world viewport shows. This alpha-bit reading is inferred from the format and the hint names, not traced into the plugin. With it off, the canvas is a fully opaque 640x480 block.
8. Full-screen 2D screens (inventory/character, map, main menu, load/save, options) use the same path. SGP's FRAME_BUFFER / ghFrameBuffer lock goes to LockPrimarySurface 0x421F70 (23 call sites, including 0x402BA1 in LockVideoSurface). So every 2D screen is blitted into the same 640x480 surface and shown through the canvas in the overlay0 pass of RenderFrame (RenderFrame has 50 call sites across all screens).
   - Extra 2D items are separate textured quads in other scenes that use the same overlay camera: portraits, icons and tooltips (g_scene_user / prerender, Video2DRectToPolygon 0x424280); square sprites (g_scene_square, view plane top 0.75, so they assume a 4:3 viewport); automap polygons (g_scene_fullscreen with SetOverlayViewport 0x429200, called from 0x57F001); the cursor (g_cursor_scene). All of them depend on the same viewport.
   - Bink videos played in game go through the canvas too (decomp: CopyFrameToPrimarySurface + InvalidateRegion).
   - The exception is the intro video: BeginVideoPresentation 0x423390 (called from 0x5AE67E) closes the SurRender window, calls SetCooperativeLevel(hwnd, 0x11 EXCLUSIVE|FULLSCREEN) and SetDisplayMode(640, 480, 16), and Bink writes straight to a real primary surface. FinishVideoPresentation 0x4234A0 restores.
9. Which single place decides the on-screen rectangle of the 2D layer: the srGERD viewport current at the moment RenderScene runs the 2D scenes. The one function every 2D pass goes through is RenderScene 0x427850, and the overlay/square cameras (globals 0x659670 / 0x659674) identify the 2D passes cleanly. The world passes go through the same function with camera = g_world->camera (+0x44) or the secondary world camera, and vp = 0x6595E8.
10. What fills the side bars if the canvas is held to 4:3: the game never clears the whole frame, because in stock play the opaque canvas always covers everything outside the 3D viewport. The only clear (0x4269FB) is scissored to g_viewport and conditional. So bars would show whatever the back buffer holds: the Hor+ world if the 3D subsystem draws full width, otherwise stale frames. This is inferred; whether srDD beginFrame (srDD vtable +0x28) clears was not checked. The patch has to fill them itself: let the world show in the main game (alpha test on), and clear the bars to black on opaque 2D screens (alpha test off, i.e. (node+0x140 & 0x800000) == 0).

functions.name: stSurface2D::DrawTiles
functions.role: Draws the 640x480 canvas as 5x4 textured quads (128x128 textures) in normalized 0..1 coordinates under an ortho(0,1,1,0,0,1) projection. Sets no viewport, so the canvas fills whatever srGERD viewport is current.
functions.key_details: __thiscall(ecx = stSurface2D*, [esp+4] = srGERD*), ret 4. The bytes before it are the previous function's ret 8 + nop. Calls via the IAT: getLocation 0x5EB79C, matrixMode 0x5EB90C, pushMatrix 0x5EB908, loadIdentity 0x5EB904, ortho(NNNNNN) 0x5EB900 (args decoded 0,1,1,0,0,1), setClipState(0x3F) 0x5EB8FC, setAntiAlias 0x5EB8F8, setTexture 0x5EB8F4, drawArrays(3 = triangle strip, 0, 4) 0x5EB8F0, popMatrix 0x5EB8EC. Cull/shader/vertex/texcoord pointer setters are inlined as writes to gerd+0x1648/+0x1FF8/+0x21C0..+0x2228. z = -0.1 (0xBDCCCCCD). Node fields: +0x13C, +0x140 (shader, 0x800000 = alpha test), +0x148 cols, +0x14C rows, +0x15C tiles, +0x160/+0x164 tile_u/v, +0x170 texcoords. The only caller is process 0x47E0F0 (call at 0x47E0F7).

functions.name: stSurface2D::process
functions.role: Scene-graph render callback of the canvas node; passes info.renderer to DrawTiles.
functions.key_details: Referenced only from vtable slot 0x5EC76C (the slot before it, 0x5EC768, holds traverse 0x4D6540). No code calls it directly. The decomp's PresentMenuOverlayFrame has no retail counterpart (no direct reference found).

functions.name: RenderScene
functions.role: Renders one srScene with a camera. If vp640 is non-NULL, sets viewport and scissor to vp*W/640, vp*H/480 and restores (0,0,W,H) afterwards; if NULL, leaves the viewport untouched. Every 2D overlay pass and the world passes go through it, so this is the place that decides where on screen each layer lands.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(srScene*, srCamera*, const int* vp640[left,top,right,bottom], bool preserve_fog), plain ret. Returns early if scene is NULL or getChildCount() == 0. IAT: getWidth 0x5EBB04, getHeight 0x5EB5F4, getChildCount 0x5EB674, setViewPort 0x5EB604, setScissor 0x5EB640, srScene::render 0x5EB658, flushRenderers 0x5EB654. Scaling uses unsigned mull magic (0xCCCCCCCD>>9 = /640, 0x88888889>>8 = /480), so negative coordinates are not allowed. 11 call sites, all inside RenderFrame (0x426A3A, 0x426A57, 0x426A9F, 0x426BC6, 0x426C0D, 0x426C4F, 0x426C68, 0x426C7E, 0x426C99, 0x426CC0, 0x426CE3).

functions.name: RenderFrame
functions.role: Draws one whole frame. Fixed order: FlushDirtyTiles, beginFrame, optional scissored clear of g_viewport, 2 prerender scenes, sky world, world (g_viewport), fullscreen scene (if not last), overlay0 (the canvas), user, square, fullscreen (if last), cursor, endFrame.
functions.key_details: Gate: g_video_active 0x659710. The clear branch 0x42692C-0x426A1D uses scissor g_viewport*W/640 (signed imul) and clear(3). Overlay gate 0x603C6D; fullscreen-last flag 0x603C4C (set via 0x4298E0); g_overlay_viewport 0x659668; cameras: overlay 0x659670, square 0x659674; scenes: user 0x659640, fullscreen 0x659644, prerender0/1 0x65964C/0x659650, overlay0 0x659654, square 0x65965C, cursor 0x659684; world 0x659AB4 (+0x3C scene, +0x44 camera); secondary world 0x659AB8. 50 call sites across the screens. A jmp at 0x4229C0 also lands here.

functions.name: FlushDirtyTiles
functions.role: Locks the 640x480 sysmem surface, merges dirty 8x8 cells (bit 0x40 in an 80x60 byte array at 0x652DDC) into rectangles, and uploads them to the canvas textures through stSurface2D::updateRectangle.
functions.key_details: Skips if g_dirty_tile_count 0x6596D8 == 0. DDLockSurface wrapper 0x40F100 / unlock 0x40F150 on 0x6596A8. Calls 0x47E450 with (g_gerd, lpSurface, pitch, x0*8, y0*8, x1*8, y1*8). Only caller: RenderFrame 0x4268C2. Works only in the 640x480 space, so the patch does not need to touch it.

functions.name: InitializePrimaryDirectDrawSurface
functions.role: DirectDrawCreate, QI to IDirectDraw2, SetCooperativeLevel(NULL, DDSCL_NORMAL = 8), creates the 640x480 16-bpp OFFSCREENPLAIN|SYSTEMMEMORY surface that backs the canvas, QI to IDirectDrawSurface2 into 0x6596A8, zero-fills it.
functions.key_details: DDSD flags 0x1007, caps 0x840, width 0x280, height 0x1E0, bpp 0x10, masks from 0x650F4A/4C/4E. No display-mode change here, so it is harmless for goal 1. Caller 0x421C40 (InitializeVideoManager).

functions.name: InitializeRendererSceneObjects
functions.role: Creates the 2D scenes and cameras (overlay camera view plane 0..1 x 0..1; square camera 0..1 x 0..0.75), wraps the sysmem surface as srColorSurface type 9 (640x480, real pitch) and builds g_surface_node = stSurface2D(surf, 640, 480, g_scene_overlay0, 128).
functions.key_details: srColorSurface ctor via IAT 0x5EB4DC at 0x423CE9 (push 9, 0x280, 0x1E0, pitch). stSurface2D ctor 0x47DAE0 called at 0x423D61 with parent [0x659654]. Stores 0x659664 at 0x423D73. If the renderer name contains GLIDE, calls enableTextureUpdateFlags(1) 0x47E5B0.

functions.name: stSurface2D::stSurface2D
functions.role: Constructor of the canvas node: computes the tile grid and creates the 128x128 stTexture2D tiles with clamp wrap.
functions.key_details: Mentioned for the layout only; no hook needed.

functions.name: stSurface2D::updateRectangle
functions.role: For each tile overlapping a dirty rectangle, calls srGERD::setTextureSubImage (partial texture upload).
functions.key_details: __thiscall(this, srGERD*, void* bits, long pitch, l, t, r, b). Pure 640-space; no hook needed. Good breakpoint for proving that a screen draws through the canvas.

functions.name: stSurface2D::setAlphaTestEnabled
functions.role: Turns the canvas between opaque and 1-bit-alpha (alpha test) modes: ORs or ANDs 0x800000 in shader bits +0x140, and toggles each tile's hints (enableHint/disableHint IAT 0x5EB5B4/0x5EB910) and invalidates them.
functions.key_details: Only caller: wrapper SetPrimarySurfaceTextureHint2Enabled 0x425570 (call at 0x42557F). Read node+0x140 & 0x800000 to tell whether the current screen is a see-through HUD (main game) or an opaque full-screen 2D screen.

functions.name: SetPrimarySurfaceTextureHint2Enabled
functions.role: cdecl wrapper: g_surface_node->setAlphaTestEnabled(bool).
functions.key_details: 15 callers (0x55FA88, 0x560C23, 0x560DFD, 0x560FF1, 0x565C70, 0x5661B6, 0x566729, 0x56882C, 0x57EAEC, 0x590F50, 0x5A395E, 0x5A9B7B, 0x5B177B, 0x5BDE70, 0x5C2E0E). Per the decomp, MainGameScreen passes true and the menu screens pass false. Optional hook spot to track 'opaque 2D screen' state.

functions.name: SetOverlayViewport
functions.role: Stores the 640-space rect pointer used for g_scene_fullscreen and g_scene_square.
functions.key_details: Only caller 0x57F001 (automap per the decomp). The confinement hook must map this rect through s/offX as well.

functions.name: SetFullscreenSceneLast
functions.role: Sets byte 0x603C4C, which decides whether g_scene_fullscreen is drawn before or after the canvas.
functions.key_details: Callers 0x56B4EF, 0x56B6DB, 0x56B918, 0x5A666B, 0x5A681B. Shows that some full-screen elements (automap, review-character 3D bits) are quads drawn under the canvas.

functions.name: SetSurfaceScale
functions.role: Quality option: shifts canvas texcoords by 0.5 texel (stSurface2D::setScale 0x47E560) and stores g_surface_scale 0x659680.
functions.key_details: Not needed for confinement. A non-integer s (for example 1080/480 = 2.25) plus bilinear filtering may show the same seams between tiles as the stock game at non-640 resolutions.

functions.name: LockPrimarySurface
functions.role: Locks the 640x480 sysmem canvas surface and returns pixels and pitch. SGP FRAME_BUFFER locks resolve here, which proves that all full-screen 2D screens draw into the canvas.
functions.key_details: 23 call sites, including 0x402BA1/0x402BF7 (LockVideoSurface FRAME_BUFFER path) and 0x5E3079 (Bink CopyFrameToPrimarySurface).

functions.name: BeginVideoPresentation
functions.role: Intro Bink path that skips the canvas: closeWindow + deleteContext on g_gerd, SetCooperativeLevel(ghWindow, 0x11), SetDisplayMode(640,480,16), creates a real DDSCAPS_PRIMARYSURFACE for Bink.
functions.key_details: Only caller 0x5AE67E (IntroScreen). Undone by FinishVideoPresentation 0x4234A0 (callers 0x5AE834/0x5AE84D/0x5AE94A). Belongs to the borderless/Bink subsystem (goal 1); listed here because it is the one 2D presentation that does not use the canvas.

functions.name: srGERD::setViewPort (sr.dll export)
functions.role: Stores viewport left/top/right/bottom at gerd+0x1638/0x163C/0x1640/0x1644 (width/height clamped to at least 1 and to getWidth/getHeight) and sets dirty bit 0x80 in gerd+0x24; applied later by applyViewStateChanges.
functions.key_details: Non-virtual __thiscall(ULONG x, y, w, h), ret 0x10. Wiz8 IAT slot 0x5EB604. setScissor 0x1001D580 (IAT 0x5EB640) stores at +0x1628..0x1634. getWidth 0x1001D020 = [ecx+0x380], getHeight 0x1001D0A0 = [ecx+0x384]. clear 0x1001D30? no: clear is 0x10020D30 (flags 1 color, 2 depth) and goes through applyViewStateChanges, so it respects viewport/scissor. getClearColor 0x1001CB40, setClearColor(MMMM) 0x1001CB00. First 16 bytes not read separately (the address comes from the export table).

hook_points.change: MinHook detour with the same cdecl signature. If camera == *(srCamera**)0x659670 (overlay) or *(srCamera**)0x659674 (square): W = [gerd+0x380], H = [gerd+0x384], s = H/480.0, offX = (W - 640*s)/2. Pixel rect = vp ? (offX + vp[0]*s, vp[1]*s, (vp[2]-vp[0])*s, (vp[3]-vp[1])*s) : (offX, 0, 640*s, H). Call srGERD::setViewPort and setScissor on *(srGERD**)0x659634 with that rect (resolve '?setViewPort@srGERD@@QAEXKKKK@Z' / '?setScissor@srGERD@@QAEXKKKK@Z' by GetProcAddress on sr.dll and call as __attribute__((thiscall))). Then call the trampoline with vp = NULL, so the original does not overwrite the rect. Afterwards restore setViewPort/setScissor(0, 0, W, H). For other cameras (world/sky), pass through untouched; the 3D subsystem handles them. Fast path: if W*3 == H*4, call through unchanged.
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 2. Covers the canvas (overlay0), sprites/tooltips/portraits (user, prerender), square sprites (they need a 4:3 viewport because the square camera top is 0.75), automap quads (fullscreen with g_overlay_viewport) and the cursor scene in one place. Also defines the mapping that goal 4 must invert: vx = (px - offX)/s, vy = py/s.
hook_points.risks: Prologue is sub esp,18 + mov ecx,[0x659634] (9 bytes, no relative operands), so it is safe for MinHook. Rounding: use the same integer rect for every 2D scene so sprites and canvas line up. PositionToolTipNode 0x4255F0 snaps tooltip positions to the full-W pixel grid (slight sub-pixel blur only). RenderWorldToSurface 0x426F80 and SetAutomapScaledViewport 0x425C90 call setViewPort directly, not through RenderScene, so they are not affected (3D subsystem). The scene getChildCount()==0 early-out in the original still runs after the hook has set the viewport, so always restore in the hook.

hook_points.target: Side-bar fill inside the RenderScene detour (before the canvas pass)
hook_points.change: Before rendering g_scene_overlay0: if (*(DWORD*)(*(BYTE**)0x659664 + 0x140) & 0x800000) == 0 (opaque 2D screen), save the clear colour (getClearColor), setClearColor(0,0,0,1), setScissor to the left bar (0, 0, offX, H) and clear(COLOR = 1), same for the right bar (offX + 640s, 0, W - that, H), then restore the clear colour and scissor. If alpha test is on (main-game HUD), leave the bars to the full-width Hor+ world from goal 3, or clear them the same way if the 3D hook is not active. Also, as a safety net, clear the bars once per frame at the first prerender call (return address 0x426A3F) so stale content can never appear.
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 2 (clean pillarbox bars). Works with goal 3 (world visible in the bars during gameplay).
hook_points.risks: srGERD::clear takes srFlags by reference (pass a pointer to a DWORD 1). It is honoured only between beginFrame and endFrame, which is true inside RenderFrame. Must not run during RenderWorldToSurface (it does not use RenderScene, so it is safe). Whether opaque menus should show the world in the bars is a design choice; the alpha-test bit is the dependable signal.

hook_points.change: Wrap with __thiscall: setViewPort(offX, 0, 640s, H) before the original and restore after. Alternatively change the ortho there, but a viewport is simpler.
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 2, but covers only the canvas. Sprites in user/square/fullscreen/cursor scenes would still be stretched, so this is only useful for A/B testing.
hook_points.risks: Leaves the sprite layers misaligned with the canvas. Prologue sub esp,58; push ebx; push ebp (5 bytes) is fine for MinHook.

hook_points.change: Global choke point alternative: remap any call made while a 2D scene is being rendered. Not recommended: the world and RenderWorldToSurface use it too, so a return-address or state filter would be needed. Better used only as a read-only probe.
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 2 / goal 3 diagnostics
hook_points.risks: Also used inside sr.dll itself. Remapping it globally would break the 3D Hor+ logic and screenshot/automap rendering.

hook_points.change: Optional: record the bool in a DLL global (g_is_hud_transparent) to drive the side-bar policy and the mouse clamping policy, instead of reading node+0x140 each frame.
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 2 bar policy, and goal 4 (clamp the cursor to the 4:3 block on opaque screens)
hook_points.risks: Trivial 16-byte function; MinHook needs 5 bytes: mov ecx,[abs] (6 bytes), fine. Reading node+0x140 directly is equivalent and needs no hook.

hook_points.change: Hand-off to the borderless/Bink subsystem: this path switches to exclusive fullscreen at 640x480 and skips the canvas, so it needs its own replacement (for example, play the intro through the in-game canvas path with m_target = NULL, or stub the mode switch).
hook_points.serves_goal: Goal 1
hook_points.risks: Out of scope for the canvas; listed so the other agent does not assume every video goes through the canvas.

runtime_checks: Viewport during the canvas draw: bp 0x47E100. On hit, g = [0x659634]; dump dword [g+0x1638],[g+0x163C],[g+0x1640],[g+0x1644] (expect 0, 0, W, H) and [g+0x380]/[g+0x384] (W/H). Also check ecx = [0x659664], [ecx+0x148] = 5, [ecx+0x14C] = 4, [ecx+0x150] = 0x14, float [ecx+0x160] = 0.2, [ecx+0x164] = 0.26667.
Ortho args: bp 0x47E152 (call to ortho). Stack holds 6 doubles: 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1 (ESP+0 = left).

Draw order: conditional-log bp at 0x427850 with log text 'scene={[esp+4]} cam={[esp+8]} vp={[esp+C]} ret={[esp]}' for one frame. Compare with [0x65964C],[0x659650],[0x659654] (overlay0 = canvas),[0x659640],[0x65965C],[0x659644],[0x659684] and the world scene [[0x659AB4]+0x3C]. Expect the order prerender, prerender, (sky), world, (fullscreen), overlay0, user, square, (fullscreen), cursor.

Live confinement experiment (no code): bp 0x47E100, then in the command bar set dword [g+0x1638] = W/8, [g+0x1640] = W - W/8 and 'or dword [g+0x24], 0x80', then run. The canvas should squeeze horizontally into the middle. The change persists for user/cursor until a RenderScene call with non-NULL vp resets it. Check whether the bars show stale frames: this tells whether the backend clears per frame and answers the side-bar open question.

Canvas is the only route for full-screen screens: open inventory/character/options/load-save with a bp on 0x47E450 (updateRectangle). It must fire when the screen repaints. A bp on 0x421F70 (LockPrimarySurface) shows the blits into the 640x480 surface.

Alpha test state per screen: bp 0x47E370 and log byte [esp+4] plus the caller. Enter the main game (expect 1) and the character/journal/options screens (expect 0). Then at any frame read dword [[0x659664]+0x140] & 0x800000.

World shows through holes: in the main game, while on a bp at 0x426C68 (the overlay0 call), set dword [0x603C6D] (byte) = 0 for one frame, or skip the call. The HUD disappears and the world plus the prerender layers remain. Conversely, patch [[0x659664]+0x140] &= ~0x800000 and see the 3D view area turn black.

Intro video skips the canvas: bp 0x423390. It should hit only from 0x5AE67E during the intro, and the next instruction should show the SetDisplayMode(640,480,16) call at 0x4233E4. No hit when in-game videos play; those should hit 0x5E3079 (LockPrimarySurface from Bink) instead.
g_overlay_viewport users: bp 0x429200 while opening the automap; log [esp+4] and dump 4 dwords there (640-space rect).
open_questions: Does srDD_DirectX7 beginFrame (srDD vtable +0x28, called from sr.dll 0x1001A7F6) or the world scene render clear the whole colour buffer each frame? Not traced. The answer decides whether the side bars need an explicit clear even during gameplay.

Is the canvas alpha really 'top bit of ARGB1555 = 0 means discarded' under shader bits 0x100A017|0x800000 in the DX7 plugin? Inferred from the hint names (ONE_BIT_ALPHA/NO_ALPHA) and the surface type 9. Confirm with the live experiment above.

Do any 2D quads use their own camera or viewport outside RenderScene, for example scenes rendered from screen code via srScene::render (IAT 0x5EB658) directly? Only RenderFrame's calls to RenderScene and RenderWorldToSurface were checked. An xref of all 'call [0x5EB658]' sites would close this.
Depth: the canvas is drawn at z = -0.1 with near 0 / far 1 and clip state 0x3F. Whether it depth-tests against the world was not checked. It only matters if the 3D hook changes depth ranges.

Should the bars on opaque menu screens show the world when g_world_render_enabled is still 1 (for example ReviewCharacterScreen sets it back to 1)? This is a policy decision; the alpha-test bit is the suggested switch.

title: 3D viewport, scissor and field of view

analysis.group: 3D viewport, scissor and field of view
analysis.summary:
All addresses below were checked against the real bytes of Wiz8.exe (SHA-256 18A74FF6…20D2, re-hashed during this run) and sr.dll (SHA-256 CEC1CAF8…6165). The decompilation's names and logic match what the bytes do at every function checked.

1) The 3D view rectangle in 640x480 units comes from a table at 0x647D30 (initialized .data, 7 entries of 16 bytes, each 4 ints: left, top, right, bottom, right/bottom exclusive). Values read from the file: mode0 {23,18,617,450}, mode1 {23,18,617,358}, mode2 {128,18,512,358}, mode3 {128,18,512,279}, mode4 {128,18,512,450}, mode5 {128,18,512,416}, mode6 {23,18,617,416}. SetViewportMode 0x5618F0 indexes the table (shl 4 + 0x647D30), sets the click region 0xE6 and calls SetViewport 0x426250(l,t,r,b). SetViewport stores g_viewport 0x6595E8 = {left, top, right+1, bottom+1} as ints in 640x480 units. Menus call SetViewport(0,0,640,480).

2) Converting to pixels: there is no float scaling. Every site computes v*W/640 and v*H/480 with integer magic-number division. W and H come from srGERD::getWidth/getHeight (IAT 0x5EBB04 / 0x5EB5F4, called on g_gerd = *(0x659634)). The globals 0x603C3C/0x603C40 are NOT used here: they are the configured display mode (atoi'd, then passed to srGERD::getDisplayMode at 0x42288F). That is why RenderScene does not touch 1/640.
- RenderScene 0x427850 uses unsigned 'mul': 0xCCCCCCCD then shr 9 means /640, 0x88888889 then shr 8 means /480. If viewport != NULL it calls setViewPort (IAT 0x5EB604, call at 0x427900, returns to 0x427906) and setScissor (IAT 0x5EB640, call at 0x427953, returns to 0x427959) with (left, top, width, height) in pixels. It then calls srScene::render (0x5EB658) and flushRenderers (0x5EB654), and restores (0,0,W,H) at 0x427A04 / 0x427A16.
- RenderFrame 0x426790 (also reached through a jmp thunk at 0x4229C0) has a 'clear the 3D rect' branch at 0x42692C..0x426A1D. It uses signed imul: 0x66666667 sar 8 means /640, 0x88888889 plus add, sar 8 means /480. It sets the scissor from g_viewport (call *ebx at 0x4269E6, returns to 0x4269E8), clears colour and depth (0x5EB63C), then restores the scissor to the full screen (0x426A1D, returns to 0x426A1F).
- RenderFrame calls RenderScene with &g_viewport (push 0x6595E8) for the sky/secondary world (0x426A9F) and the main world (0x426BC6 with picking, 0x426C0D without). Overlay scenes are drawn with viewport NULL or with g_overlay_viewport *(0x659668), which is set only by SetOverlayViewport 0x429200 (automap).
- SetAutomapScaledViewport 0x425C90 and SetWorldScaledViewport 0x425DA0 (callers: automap 0x57EB6C, BuildRegionLinks 0x4315E4/0x431BC9) call setViewPort directly and also write g_viewport.
- RenderWorldToSurface 0x426F80 (used by save screenshots and the automap backdrop) sets a full scissor (0x426FE1), then one shared setViewPort at 0x4270EB (returns to 0x4270F1). It takes either the rect argument or g_viewport.

3) Field of view: SetViewport 0x426250 is the only place that sets the world projection. When g_world *(0x659AB4) and its camera (+0x44) exist, it calls srCamera::setViewPlane(double,double) (IAT 0x5EB60C) with 85° and 71° in radians (pi 0x5EBD00 * 1/180 0x5EBCF8 * floats 85.0 @0x5EBF48 and 71.0 @0x5EBF4C). In sr.dll (0x10048920) that builds a symmetric rect {-tan(a/2), -tan(b/2), tan(a/2), tan(b/2)} at distance 1. So 85° is the horizontal and 71° the vertical FOV of the WHOLE 640x480 virtual screen. The aspect is tan42.5/tan35.5 = 1.285, not 1.333; no 1.333 constant exists.

SetViewport then reads the plane back (getViewPlane, IAT 0x5EB608) and crops it to the viewport's share of the screen, using fractions l/640, (r+1)/640, t/480, (b+1)/480 (the floats at 0x5EBB1C and 0x5EBB20, with 1.0 at 0x5EBC30 for the vertical flip). This gives an off-centre sub-frustum, set with setViewPlane(Rect, 1.0) (IAT 0x5EB4EC loaded into esi at 0x426340). The calls are at 0x4263A7 (world camera, returns to 0x4263A9) and 0x4263C1 (secondary/sky camera *(0x659AB8)+0x44, returns to 0x4263C3). If the sway flag byte 0x652DA4 is set, it then calls SetCameraSwayMode 0x450080(camera, 1). sr.dll srCamera::processPush 0x10047E50 builds the GERD frustum (or ortho) from the view plane on every render, so plane changes apply on the next frame.

Other places that write or read the plane:
- GDCamera::CreateOrAttachCamera 0x476440 sets a default 90x90 symmetric plane (0x476555).
- W8Octree::BuildRegionLinks 0x4314C0 saves getHorizontal/VerticalFOV, sets 120x120, then restores a symmetric plane.
- SetCameraSwayMode 0x450080 captures getHorizontal/VerticalFOV and drives a symmetric setViewPlane(h,v) each frame.
- W8Octree::UpdateCameraVisibility 0x42F7E0 culls with getHorizontalFOV/getVerticalFOV, which sr.dll computes from the current plane: atan(right) - atan(left).
- srCamera::project (gameplay visibility checks 0x44E3A0, 0x53A060, 0x4BE940) uses the plane too.
- The 2D overlay and square cameras use planes {0,0,1,1} and {0,0,1,0.75} (InitializeRendererSceneObjects 0x423500). Those belong to the 2D group.

4) Hor+ plan. Keep g_viewport in 640x480 units unchanged. RenderScene uses unsigned maths, and the cursor/pick tests at 0x428030, 0x428070, 0x428230 and in RenderFrame compare against it. Define s = H/480, offX = (W - 640*s)/2, VL = -offX/s, VR = 640 + offX/s.
- (a) Viewport and scissor for the world passes only: x = 0, width = W. Vertical stays t*H/480, which already equals t*s.
- (b) Camera plane: widen it horizontally on the same linear mapping. With k = (pr - pl)/((R+1) - L): new left = pl + k*(VL - L), new right = pl + k*(VR - L). Top and bottom stay unchanged, so the vertical FOV is kept. For 16:9 the horizontal FOV of the full plane goes from 85° to about 101°.
- (c) Pick: remap the clip-space x for the wider viewport.
- (d) The RenderFrame clear scissor must be widened the same way.
- Recommended: widen only when the 3D rect touches the 4:3 edges (modes 0, 1, 6 with L=23, R=617). Keep modes 2-5 (L=128, R=512, between big side panels) pillarboxed.
Sway, octree culling and the BuildRegionLinks restore all read the widened plane back and follow it automatically. Gameplay visibility checks will also see the wider view (inferred side effect).

functions.role: Draws one srScene with a camera. If the viewport pointer is non-NULL it converts that 640x480-unit rect to pixels, sets the GERD viewport and scissor, renders, then restores a full-screen viewport and scissor.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(srScene* scene [esp+4], srCamera* cam [+8], const int* vp [+0xC], bool preserve_fog [+0x10]); plain ret, the caller cleans the stack. W = g_gerd->getWidth() (IAT 0x5EBB04), H = getHeight() (IAT 0x5EB5F4), g_gerd = *(0x659634). Unsigned mul: 0xCCCCCCCD then shr 9 is /640, 0x88888889 then shr 8 is /480. setViewPort(left,top,width,height): call *0x5EB604 at 0x427900, returns to 0x427906. setScissor: call *0x5EB640 at 0x427953, returns to 0x427959. Render: srScene::render *0x5EB658 at 0x4279E1, then flushRenderers *0x5EB654. Restore (0,0,W,H): setViewPort at 0x427A04 (returns to 0x427A0A), setScissor at 0x427A16 (returns to 0x427A1C). The world and sky passes pass vp == 0x6595E8 (&g_viewport). Negative vp values would break because of the unsigned arithmetic.

functions.name: RenderFrame
callers: 0x004229C0 (jmp thunk, itself called from 0x5BCF71 and jumped to from 0x5A4520)
functions.role: Renders one whole frame. When the world is blacked out it clears only the 3D rect (scissor from g_viewport). It then draws the prerender pages, the sky world and the main world (with an optional pick), then the overlays and cursor, and ends the frame.
functions.key_details: Clear branch 0x42692C..0x426A1D uses signed imul: 0x66666667 sar 8 is /640, 0x88888889 plus add, sar 8 is /480. setScissor (ebx = *0x5EB640): call at 0x4269E6, returns to 0x4269E8. clear (0x5EB63C, flags 3) at 0x4269FB. Full-screen scissor restore at 0x426A1D, returns to 0x426A1F. Sky pass: RenderScene(*(0x659AB8)+0x3C scene, +0x44 camera, 0x6595E8, 0) at 0x426A9F, gated by bytes 0x603C6C and 0x65970C. World pass at 0x426BC6 (pick, preserve_fog=1) or 0x426C0D, gated by g_world 0x659AB4 and byte 0x65970D. The pick branch runs when byte 0x603C38 is set and the cursor (0x6596BC+0x654AD0, 0x6596C0+0x654AD4) lies inside g_viewport. It builds the clip-space pick x = (cx - halfw - L)/halfw and y = -(cy - halfh - T)/halfh, z = 1. Then setPickKey 0x5EB634, pushPick 0x5EB630 (call at 0x426BAC, returns to 0x426BB2), popPick 0x5EB62C. Overlays use the viewport pointer *(0x659668) (g_overlay_viewport) or NULL.

functions.name: SetViewport (sets g_viewport and the world camera view plane, i.e. the FOV)
functions.role: Stores g_viewport = {l, t, r+1, b+1} in 640x480 units. Rebuilds the world camera (and sky camera) projection: a full-screen 85 by 71 degree plane, cropped to the viewport's share of the screen, giving an off-centre frustum. This is THE FOV function.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(int l, int t, int r, int b). Optional flush: if g_gerd and byte 0x603C3A, call *0x5EB610. Fractions use 1/640 (0x5EBB1C) and 1/480 (0x5EBB20). Writes 0x6595E8/EC/F0/F4. setViewPlane(double h, double v), IAT 0x5EB60C, call at 0x426310: h = pi(0x5EBD00) * 1/180(0x5EBCF8) * 85.0f(0x5EBF48), v = same with 71.0f(0x5EBF4C). getViewPlane, IAT 0x5EB608, call at 0x426328. Crop: plane.l = vl + fl*(vr - vl), plane.r likewise; plane.b = vb + (1 - fb)*(vt - vb) and plane.t likewise, with 1.0 at 0x5EBC30. setViewPlane(Rect const&, 1.0): esi = *0x5EB4EC loaded at 0x426340; world camera call at 0x4263A7 (returns to 0x4263A9), secondary camera *(0x659AB8)+0x44 call at 0x4263C1 (returns to 0x4263C3). If sway byte 0x652DA4 is set: SetCameraSwayMode(world cam, 1) at 0x4263D8. Does nothing to the camera when g_world == 0.

functions.name: SetViewportMode
functions.role: Picks one of the 7 preset 3D view rects (table 0x647D30), updates click region 0xE6 and the invalidate rect at 0x647F44..50, calls SetViewport, and caches the mode at *(0x68EDCC)+0x100.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(int mode). Early-out if the mode equals the cached one. Table at 0x647D30, 16-byte stride, ints {l,t,r,b} with r/b exclusive: {23,18,617,450}, {23,18,617,358}, {128,18,512,358}, {128,18,512,279}, {128,18,512,450}, {128,18,512,416}, {23,18,617,416}, all verified in the file. The SetRegionBounds call is 0x4F2420(0xE6, l, t, r-1, b-1).

functions.name: SetAutomapScaledViewport
functions.role: If the rect differs from g_viewport: setViewPort(rect*W/640, rect*H/480) directly, then stores the rect into g_viewport. It does not touch the camera.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(l,t,r,b). Signed magic division (0x66666667 sar 8, 0x88888889 plus add, sar 8). setViewPort call at 0x425D67 (returns to 0x425D6D). Writes 0x6595E8.. at 0x425D76. Used only by the automap.

functions.name: SetWorldScaledViewport
functions.role: Same as SetAutomapScaledViewport. Used while building region links offline at level load.
functions.key_details: setViewPort call at 0x425E8C (returns to 0x425E92). Writes g_viewport at 0x425E9B. Should be left alone (its rendering is not for display).

functions.name: RenderWorldToSurface
functions.role: Renders the world off-frame into the GERD buffer: viewport from the rect or from g_viewport. It then locks the buffer and copies it into a colour surface.
functions.key_details: cdecl uchar(srColorSurface* target, W8ScreenRect* rect, bool secondary). Uses gerd = *(0x65971C) (secondary GERD) or else *(0x659634). Full-screen setScissor at 0x426FE1 (returns to 0x426FE7). The rect and g_viewport branches merge into one setViewPort call at 0x4270EB (returns to 0x4270F1). The restore setViewPort(0,0,W,H) at 0x4271E3 (returns to 0x4271E9) happens only when rect != NULL. Render goes through srScene::render directly, not through RenderScene.

functions.name: SetCameraSwayMode
functions.role: Camera sway effect. Mode > 0 captures getHorizontalFOV/getVerticalFOV (IAT 0x5EB700/0x5EB6FC, calls at 0x4500A6/0x4500C2) in degrees. Each update then calls setViewPlane(h + 0.75*sin, v + 0.63*sin) (symmetric, IAT 0x5EB60C at 0x4501CE/0x450202). Mode < 0 restores the captured FOV.
functions.key_details: cdecl void(srCamera*, int). It rebuilds a SYMMETRIC plane from the total FOV, so once SetViewport has widened the plane, sway automatically keeps the Hor+ width. Any hook on setViewPlane(double,double) must not widen again (that would widen twice).

functions.name: W8Octree::UpdateCameraVisibility
functions.role: Visibility culling of octree regions: reads the world camera's getHorizontalFOV/getVerticalFOV (calls at 0x42F847/0x42F856) and stores their cosines.
functions.key_details: thiscall. sr.dll getHorizontalFOV 0x10048AB0 = atan(plane.right/d) - atan(plane.left/d), computed from the live plane. A widened plane therefore widens culling automatically, with nothing to hook. That the angle is used as a cone half-angle is inferred from the decomp and not verified in bytes.

functions.name: W8Octree::BuildRegionLinks
functions.role: Level-load preprocessing. Saves the H/V FOV (0x431648/0x431655), sets a 120x120 plane (0x431676, constant 2.094395102), renders region links through SetWorldScaledViewport, then restores a symmetric setViewPlane(savedH, savedV) at 0x431AB8.
functions.key_details: After this runs, the world camera plane is symmetric (the off-centre crop is lost) until SetViewport runs again. That is original behaviour. A Hor+ widening done inside SetViewport survives this as a symmetric plane with the widened total FOV.

functions.name: GDCamera::CreateOrAttachCamera
functions.first_bytes_hex: 55 8b ec 83 e4 f8 6a ff 68 bb 4e 5e 00 64 a1 00
functions.role: Creates the 'Sirtech Camera' with clip range 250..75000 and a default symmetric 90x90 degree plane (setViewPlane at 0x476555; pi 0x5EC538 * 1/180 double 0x5EC300 * 90.0 0x5EC568).
functions.key_details: The real 85/71 crop is applied only when SetViewport runs after the world exists (g_world is written at 0x451294).

functions.name: GetScaledViewportBounds
functions.role: Returns g_viewport multiplied by (1/640, 1/480).
functions.key_details: Debug wireframe only, not needed for the patch.

functions.name: GetCursorPositionInViewport / IsCursorInsideViewport / IsCursorImageInsideViewport
functions.role: Cursor-in-3D-view tests in 640x480 units against g_viewport. The siblings are at 0x428070 (8b 0d bc 96 65 00 ...) and 0x428030 (a1 d0 4a 65 00 3b 05 e8 95 65 00 ...).
functions.key_details: Cursor = 0x6596BC + 0x654AD0 (x), 0x6596C0 + 0x654AD4 (y), virtual units. These are why g_viewport must stay in virtual units.

functions.name: sr.dll srCamera::setViewPlane(double,double)
functions.first_bytes_hex: dd 05 30 6e 07 10 83 ec 28 d9 e0 8b d1 d9 c0 dd
functions.role: Clamps both angles to [-pi, pi] (0x10076E30). Sets plane = {-tan(a/2), -tan(b/2), tan(a/2), tan(b/2)} (0.5 at 0x10075330) at +0x140..+0x158 and distance 1.0 at +0x160.
functions.key_details: thiscall, retn 0x10. Argument a is horizontal, b is vertical. Rect layout is {left, bottom, right, top} as doubles.

functions.name: sr.dll srCamera::setViewPlane(Rect const&, double)
functions.role: Sets an arbitrary (possibly off-centre) view plane and distance.
functions.key_details: thiscall, args (Rect* [esp+4], double [esp+8]). Its second instruction holds an absolute address; that is fine for a MinHook trampoline. A better hook point is the Wiz8 IAT slot 0x5EB4EC: SetViewport loads it into esi at 0x426340, so the slot must be patched before that runs (at DLL load).

functions.name: sr.dll srGERD::setViewPort / setScissor / pushPick
functions.role: setViewPort(x,y,w,h) clamps to the GERD size and sets a dirty flag. setScissor is at 0x1001D580 (8b 44 24 04 8b 54 24 0c 56 8b f1 8b 4c 24 0c 89). pushPick is at 0x1001DAA0 (8b c1 8b 88 ec 19 00 00 83 f9 20 73 26 56 8b 74) and pushes a Pick whose position is in clip space (NDC -1..1 over the current viewport and frustum).
functions.key_details: All thiscall, retn 0x10 (setViewPort, setScissor) and retn 4 (pushPick). getWidth 0x1001D020 = mov eax,[ecx+0x380]; ret. getHeight 0x1001D0A0 = mov eax,[ecx+0x384]; ret. srCamera::processPush 0x10047E50 (55 8b ec 83 e4 f8 81 ec 5c 01 00 00 ...) calls getViewPlane, then frustum or ortho (flag at +0x138 bit 0), on every render.

hook_points.target: srCamera::setViewPlane(Rect const&, double) via the Wiz8 IAT slot
hook_points.address: 0x005EB4EC (IAT slot); filter on return address 0x004263A9 (world cam) and 0x004263C3 (sky cam)
hook_points.change: Replace the slot with our thunk (thiscall: ecx = camera, [esp+4] = Rect*, [esp+8] = double). If the return address is 0x4263A9 or 0x4263C3, Hor+ is on and the current g_viewport (L = *0x6595E8, R1 = *0x6595F0, already updated by SetViewport) touches the edges (L <= 23 and R1 >= 618): build a copy of the rect with left' = l + k*(VL - L) and right' = l + k*(VR - L). Here k = (r - l)/(R1 - L), VL = -offX/s, VR = 640 + offX/s, s = H/480, offX = (W - 640s)/2, and W, H come from g_gerd getWidth/getHeight. Leave bottom and top unchanged so the vertical FOV is kept. Then call the original. All other callers (overlay cameras, automap 0x5810B7) pass through unchanged.
hook_points.serves_goal: (3) Hor+ field of view. The sway (captured right after, at 0x4263D8), octree culling and the BuildRegionLinks restore all inherit the widened plane automatically.
hook_points.risks: The slot must be patched before SetViewport first runs (do it in DllMain/at version.dll load). SetViewport caches the slot value in esi at 0x426340 for the current call only, so this is fine. The return-address filter is tied to this exact exe build. Gameplay visibility checks through srCamera::project (monster/prop 'in view' at 0x53A060 and 0x44E3A0) will treat the widened view as visible; that is inherent to Hor+ (inferred).

hook_points.target: SetViewport replacement (alternative to the IAT hook above)
hook_points.change: MinHook the entry (cdecl void(int l,int t,int r,int b), standard prologue 55 8b ec 83 e4 f8). Reimplement: optional flush; store g_viewport = {l, t, r+1, b+1}; if g_world*(0x659AB4) and camera (+0x44) exist: setViewPlane(85°,71°), getViewPlane, compute the crop using horizontal fractions VL/640 and VR/640 instead of l/640 and (r+1)/640 (vertical as original); setViewPlane(rect, 1.0) on the world camera and the sky camera *(0x659AB8)+0x44; if byte 0x652DA4 is set, call 0x450080(cam, 1).
hook_points.serves_goal: (3) Hor+ FOV
hook_points.risks: Duplicates game logic (globals 0x603C3A, 0x652DA4, 0x659AB4/B8 must be exact). Easier to get subtly wrong than the IAT filter. No return-address dependence, though.

hook_points.target: RenderScene entry hook plus world-pass viewport/scissor override
hook_points.change: Hook RenderScene (cdecl, 4 args). If vp == (int*)0x6595E8 and Hor+ applies to the current g_viewport (same edge test), set a flag 'worldPass' around the call to the original. In the setViewPort/setScissor hooks (preferably Wiz8 IAT slots 0x5EB604/0x5EB640, or inline on the sr.dll exports 0x1001D410/0x1001D580), when worldPass is set and the args are not (0,0,W,H): replace x with 0 and width with W. Keep y and height (t*H/480 == t*s already). Equivalent without a flag: in the IAT hooks, override when the return address is 0x427906 or 0x427959 and *(esp of RenderScene + 0xC) == 0x6595E8. The flag is simpler.
hook_points.serves_goal: (3) 3D world across the full width behind the HUD. The same mechanism keeps the world pass out of the 2D group's pillarbox remap of setViewPort/setScissor ((2) coordination).
hook_points.risks: Must coordinate with the 2D pillarbox hook on the same setViewPort/setScissor: the world pass must bypass the 4:3 compression. The plane widening (hook 1) and viewport widening must always be applied together, or the image distorts. Modes 2-5 (128..512) should stay non-widened.

hook_points.change: In the setScissor IAT hook: if the return address is 0x4269E8 and Hor+ applies, set x = 0 and width = W (vertical unchanged). The restore at return address 0x426A1F is already full screen.
hook_points.serves_goal: (3) Correct clearing of the widened 3D area (blackout/fade frames).
hook_points.risks: Return-address based. Without it, the pillar areas keep stale pixels during world blackout.

hook_points.address: IAT 0x005EB630; only caller 0x00426BAC (return address 0x00426BB2); sr.dll export 0x1001DAA0
hook_points.change: thiscall pushPick(const Pick& p). If the world pass is widened: undo the game's NDC to get the virtual cursor x, xv = L + (p.x + 1)*(R1 - L)/2. Then recompute p.x' = 2*(xv - VL)/(VR - VL) - 1. Leave y unchanged (vertical viewport unchanged). Pass a modified copy to the original.
hook_points.serves_goal: (4) Mouse picking in the 3D view stays correct after widening
hook_points.risks: Picking is still only attempted when the cursor is inside the virtual g_viewport (RenderFrame test at 0x426ADC..0x426B2A and helpers 0x428030/0x428070/0x428230). Clicking 3D objects in the pillar areas will not work unless those tests are also extended (optional). This assumes the 2D/mouse group delivers the cursor in virtual 640x480 units (0x6596BC/0x654AD0).

hook_points.change: Hook the entry. When rect == NULL (g_viewport path) and Hor+ is active, either set worldPass so setViewPort is widened (x = 0, w = W), matching the widened plane, or temporarily give the camera the unwidened plane. Automap calls (rect = &g_automap_viewport) set their own plane at 0x5810B1 and should be left alone.
hook_points.serves_goal: (3) Undistorted save thumbnails / consistency
hook_points.risks: Low priority. The thumbnail is copied from the whole buffer with a box filter, so the widened image may look different; acceptable either way (inferred).

For mode 0, expected roughly l = -0.9163 + (23/640)*1.8326 and r = -0.9163 + (618/640)*1.8326, from tan(42.5°) = 0.9163 and tan(35.5°) = 0.7133. This confirms the 85/71 crop maths.

The horizontal FOV should widen while 71 keeps the vertical. This shows SetViewport is the only FOV source.

What W/H will srGERD::getWidth/getHeight report under borderless desktop resolution with dgVoodoo2: the backbuffer size equal to the desktop, or the configured 0x603C3C mode? All formulas here assume W, H = actual backbuffer pixels.

Automap: RenderAutomapFrame 0x581030 rewrites the world camera plane (0x5810B1) and SetAutomapScaledViewport rewrites g_viewport. Who restores the world plane on leaving the automap (presumably SetViewport through SetViewportMode)? Not traced.

analysis.summary:
The game reads the mouse through two separate paths. Neither path scales anything: one screen pixel counts as one 640x480 logical unit.

PATH A, polled position. SyncSystemCursor 0x428340 is the only caller of GetCursorPos in Wiz8.exe (call [0x5EB250] at 0x42834A).
- Fullscreen (byte g_fullscreen 0x603C39 != 0): the raw screen point is clamped to 0..640 x 0..480, with 640 and 480 included (0x42835D-0x428396). If the result differs from the stored position (dwords 0x654AD0/0x654AD4), the function calls PositionMouseCursor(x,y,1) at 0x428140, then SetCursorPos(x,y) at 0x4283CD with the logical numbers. That warp pins the OS cursor to the top-left 640x480 pixels of the screen, which matches what was seen live.
- Windowed (/WINDOW): it calls GetClientRect plus ClientToScreen on both corners. If the cursor is inside the client area: logical = screen - client top-left, with no scaling and no lower clamp, and it calls ShowCursor(FALSE). Outside the client area it calls ShowCursor(TRUE) and leaves the position unchanged (0x428428-0x4284E7).
- Clamp in PositionMouseCursor 0x428140: upper bound only, 640/480 (0x428151-0x428180). It stores 0x654AD0/D4 and moves the 2D cursor model through sr.dll srNode::setLocation (IAT 0x5EB524) as x/640 + w/1280 and 1 - y/480 - h/960. The constants at 0x5EBE90, 0x5EBE88, 0x5EBE80 and 0x5EBC30 are 1/640, 1/480, 0.5 and 1.0. The drawn cursor therefore lives in the 640x480 overlay space and follows whatever the 2D pillarbox does.
- SGPMouseGetPos 0x4284F0 (62 call sites) calls SyncSystemCursor, then returns 0x654AD0 + 0x6596BC and 0x654AD4 + 0x6596C0. The decomp calls the latter pair the cursor hotspot.

PATH B, event coordinates. Buttons and moves never go through the window procedure. WindowProcedure 0x4011E0 returns 0 for WM_MOUSEMOVE (0x4013E7 jumps to 0x401523). Button messages go to DefWindowProc; only the wheel is queued (0x40150C, QueueEvent(0x800, wParam, lParam)). The input is a thread-local WH_MOUSE hook, MouseHandler 0x401C70, installed at 0x401F58 by SetWindowsHookExA(7, 0x401C70, 0, tid); its handle is at 0x6F050C. It takes MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT.pt, which is in screen coordinates:
- Fullscreen: pt is used as is.
- Windowed: pt minus the client top-left from VideoGetClientRect 0x427A70.
- The result is truncated to 16 bits. It is stored in word globals 0x6F050A (x) and 0x6F04F8 (y) and packed as (y<<16)|x.
- The packed value is passed as uiParam to QueueEvent 0x401F90: 8 = left down, 0x10 = left up, 0x80 = right down, 0x100 = right up, 0x400 = mouse move (only when byte 0x6F04EC is set).
- The hook returns TRUE, so the message is swallowed.

So button events carry their own coordinates, taken from the hook point at the moment of the click. They are separate from the polled position. They sit in the 16-byte event record at +0xC and are read back by GetAtomCursorX/Y (0x428580/0x4285A0), which add the hotspot. Game code also reads 0x6F050A/0x6F04F8 directly (for example 0x4F20AE, 0x592669, 0x5D4DF2). Button-repeat events (0x40 left, 0x200 right) in DequeueEvent 0x402140 are the exception: their coordinates come from SGPMouseGetPos (polled path, hotspot already added).

Warps. There are six SetCursorPos call sites, all `call [0x5EB254]` and all in Wiz8.exe:
- WarpSystemCursor 0x4280C0: 0x4280D6 (fullscreen: logical x,y) and 0x42812A (windowed: client origin + logical).
- SyncSystemCursor: 0x4283CD and 0x42841B (the second is unreachable in practice).
- SetMouseCursorFromVideoObject 0x427AB0: 0x427B88 (copy of the WarpSystemCursor logic).
- SetMouseCursorHotspot 0x427F00: 0x427F92 (same copy).

The last two warp by the hotspot difference so that position + hotspot stays the same. Game callers of WarpSystemCursor pass logical values, for example (320,240) to centre the cursor at 0x4903A2 and 0x567EDB, and the saved SGPMouseGetPos point at 0x567E82.

sr.dll and srDD_DirectX7.dll import no cursor APIs. srDD does import GetClientRect and ClientToScreen, so do not hook those globally.

Minimal hooks for a centred 4:3 block, assuming g_fullscreen stays 1 inside a borderless window:
1. Wiz8.exe IAT slot for GetCursorPos (0x5EB250): screen -> logical.
2. Wiz8.exe IAT slot for SetCursorPos (0x5EB254): logical -> screen.
3. MouseHandler 0x401C70, entry hook or wrapping the proc through the SetWindowsHookExA IAT slot 0x5EB2B8: rewrite pt to logical and clamp it before the original runs.

Formulas:
- Let (cx,cy) be the client top-left on screen, s = H/480, offX = round((W - 640*s)/2).
- Screen to logical: lx = floor((sx - cx - offX)/s), ly = floor((sy - cy)/s).
- Logical to screen: sx = cx + offX + ceil(lx*s), sy = cy + ceil(ly*s). Using ceil makes the round trip exact.
- In windowed mode, add and remove the client origin the same way the game expects.

Hooking WarpSystemCursor and SyncSystemCursor alone is not enough, because 0x427B88 and 0x427F92 call SetCursorPos directly.

Separately, RenderFrame turns the logical cursor into a pick ray: normalised coordinates relative to g_viewport 0x6595E8..0x6595F4, sent to sr.dll srGERD::pushPick (IAT 0x5EB630) from about 0x426ADC-0x426BAC. With Hor+, picking stays correct only if the central 4:3 part of the widened 3D image lines up with the 2D block and the vertical FOV is unchanged (inferred). Otherwise the pick x needs rescaling at that IAT slot.

functions.name: SyncSystemCursor
functions.role: The only place the game reads the OS cursor. Fullscreen: clamps the raw screen point to 0..640 x 0..480 and, if it changed, updates the game cursor and warps the OS cursor to the clamped point. Windowed: subtracts the client top-left (no scaling), shows or hides the OS cursor depending on whether it is inside the client area, and updates the game cursor.
functions.key_details:
Preceded by 0x90 padding; sub esp,0x18 prologue. GetCursorPos [0x5EB250] at 0x42834A into local POINT at esp+8. Branches on byte 0x603C39 at 0x428350.
Fullscreen clamp at 0x42835D-0x428396: cmp 0x280 / jge -> 640, test/jle -> 0, same for 0x1E0. 640 and 480 are reachable values.
Compares with 0x654AD0/0x654AD4 at 0x42839A, then calls 0x428140(x,y,1) at 0x4283B2 and SetCursorPos(x,y) at 0x4283CD. The block at 0x4283D9-0x428427 re-tests the fullscreen flag and is effectively dead.
Windowed branch 0x428428: GetClientRect [0x5EB258] and ClientToScreen [0x5EB25C] x2 on HWND 0x6596CC. Half-open inside test [left,right) x [top,bottom). Subtracts the origin, calls 0x428140(x,y,1) at 0x4284A1, then ShowCursor [0x5EB244] toggled through byte 0x6596C4.

functions.name: PositionMouseCursor
functions.role: Stores the game cursor position in logical 640x480 space and moves the 2D cursor model in the overlay scene.
functions.key_details:
Args (int x, int y, bool resetTick), cdecl. Exits if g_mouse_surface 0x659688 is NULL.
Upper-bound-only clamp: x>640 -> 640, y>480 -> 480 (0x428155-0x428180). Writes 0x654AD0/0x654AD4; the decomp's name 'g_cursor_width/height' is wrong, these hold the cursor position.
If the cursor model 0x659694 exists: location = (x*(1/640) + surfW*(1/640)*0.5, 1 - (y*(1/480) + surfH*(1/480)*0.5), 0), using doubles 0x5EBE90 / 0x5EBE88 / 0x5EBE80 / 0x5EBC30, passed to sr.dll ?setLocation@srNode@@QAEXABV?$srVector3T@N@@@Z (IAT 0x5EB524).
If resetTick, stores GetTickCount in 0x659698. Takes no screen coordinates, so it needs no hook: the drawn cursor is placed in overlay space and is pillarboxed together with the 2D layer.

functions.name: WarpSystemCursor
functions.role: Moves the OS cursor to a logical point.
functions.key_details:
Args (int x, int y), cdecl. Fullscreen: SetCursorPos(x,y) [0x5EB254] at 0x4280D6, logical values passed straight to the OS. Windowed: GetClientRect + ClientToScreen x2, then SetCursorPos(left+x, top+y) at 0x42812A.
The first instruction is a 5-byte `mov al,[0x603C39]`, which suits MinHook. Not sufficient as the only warp hook: two other functions inline the same SetCursorPos logic.

functions.name: SGPMouseGetPos
functions.role: Polled game cursor query: syncs with the OS cursor, then returns position + hotspot in logical units.
functions.key_details: Arg POINT*. Calls 0x428340, then out.x = [0x654AD0] + [0x6596BC], out.y = [0x654AD4] + [0x6596C0]. Already logical after the GetCursorPos fix, so it needs no hook.

functions.name: MouseHandler (WH_MOUSE hook procedure)
callers: installed by SetWindowsHookExA(7, 0x401C70, 0, GetCurrentThreadId()) at 0x401F58-0x401F5F; handle stored in 0x6F050C
functions.role: Source of every click and mouse-move event. Converts MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT.pt (screen coordinates) to game coordinates without any scaling, stores it, and queues button and move events that carry their own packed coordinates.
functions.key_details:
stdcall (int code, WPARAM msg, LPARAM pMHS), ret 0xC. The preceding byte is 00 (end of a jump table), but the address is pushed as the hook proc, so this is a genuine entry. Prologue `sub esp,0x10; push ebx; push ebp` is safe for MinHook.
esi = pt.x, edi = pt.y. Calls VideoIsFullScreen 0x4229B0 (returns byte 0x603C39). Windowed: VideoGetClientRect 0x427A70 gives the client rect in screen coordinates; outside it the message is passed on. Also passed on when code<0, gfApplicationActive byte 0x6F0630 is 0, or the resizing flag 0x650DBA is set; these pass-through paths call CallNextHookEx [0x5EB2B4].
Jump table 0x401E68 for msg 0x200-0x205 (0x203 excluded): fullscreen x=pt.x, y=pt.y; windowed: subtract client left/top. Words stored to 0x6F050A (x) and 0x6F04F8 (y); packed eax = (y<<16)|(x&0xFFFF); sets 0x650DB9.
WM_MOUSEWHEEL returns 0. Second table 0x401E80 calls QueueEvent(code, 0, packed): 0x201->8 (sets 0x6F04ED), 0x202->0x10, 0x204->0x80 (sets 0x6F04E8), 0x205->0x100, 0x200->0x400 only if byte 0x6F04EC. Returns 1, so the message is eaten.
No clamp: a negative value wraps to 0xFFxx.

functions.name: QueueEvent
functions.role: Pushes a 16-byte event record into the 256-entry ring 0x6EF4E0. The record's +0xC uiParam holds the packed mouse point. Also creates double-click events.
functions.key_details: cdecl (u16 event, u32 usParam, u32 uiParam). Do NOT transform coordinates here: the button-repeat events (0x40, 0x200) already pass logical values from SGPMouseGetPos, so a transform here would apply twice.

functions.name: DequeueEvent / button repeat
functions.role: Creates button-repeat events from the polled position, then pops one event.
functions.key_details: Left repeat: QueueEvent(0x40, 0, packed(SGPMouseGetPos)) at 0x402184. Right repeat: QueueEvent(0x200, ...) at 0x4021DA. Copies a 16-byte record from 0x6EF4E0 + 16*head. Repeat coordinates include the hotspot, while hook-sourced button coordinates do not; GetAtomCursorX adds the hotspot again (inferred quirk of the original game).

functions.name: GetAtomCursorX / GetAtomCursorY
functions.role: Reads the per-event coordinates: low or high word of the record's +0xC field, plus the hotspot 0x6596BC/0x6596C0.
functions.key_details: Confirms that button events carry coordinates separately from the polled position.

functions.name: SetMouseCursorHotspot
functions.role: Changes the hotspot and warps the OS cursor by (old hotspot - new hotspot) so that position + hotspot stays the same. Contains its own SetCursorPos call.
functions.key_details: Args (short hx, short hy). New position = [0x654AD0] - hx + oldHx (same for y). Fullscreen: SetCursorPos(logical) at 0x427F92; windowed: client origin + logical. Then calls SyncSystemCursor at 0x427F98 and stores 0x6596BC/0x6596C0.

functions.name: SetMouseCursorFromVideoObject
functions.role: Changes the cursor image and hotspot, with the same inline warp as SetMouseCursorHotspot.
functions.key_details: SetCursorPos at 0x427B88 with logical coordinates in fullscreen, then SyncSystemCursor at 0x427B8E.

functions.name: VideoGetClientRect
functions.role: Client rect of HWND 0x6596CC converted to screen coordinates.
functions.key_details: GetClientRect + ClientToScreen on both corners. Used only on the windowed path of the hook.

functions.name: WindowProcedure
functions.role: Main WndProc. Does not process mouse position or buttons.
functions.key_details: msg 0x200 -> 0x401523 (returns 0). 0x20A (WM_MOUSEWHEEL) and the registered wheel message 0x6F0620 -> QueueEvent(0x800, wParam, lParam) at 0x40151B. Button messages fall to DefWindowProcA [0x5EB248], and in practice never arrive because the WH_MOUSE hook eats them.

functions.name: RenderFrame pick-ray block (inside RenderFrame 0x426790)
functions.role: Converts the logical cursor (position + hotspot) into viewport-relative normalised coordinates and sends a pick to sr.dll.
functions.key_details: Uses g_viewport 0x6595E8/EC/F0/F4 (logical left/top/right/bottom): x = (cur - left - halfW)/halfW, y = -(cur - top - halfH)/halfH. Calls srGERD::setPickKey [0x5EB634], then srGERD::pushPick(const Pick&) [0x5EB630], thiscall with ecx = 0x659634. Inferred Pick layout: +0 float x, +4 float y, +8 = 1.0f, then two zero dwords.

functions.name: ClipCursor(NULL) helper
functions.role: Releases the cursor clip and clears byte 0x650DB8.
functions.key_details: The only real ClipCursor use found. Other `call [0x5EB230]` hits (0x40BF9A, 0x4159B5, 0x419A39, ...) sit right after a ret and look like unreachable stubs (inferred).

hook_points.change:
Call the real GetCursorPos to get (sx,sy). If byte [0x603C39] != 0 (fullscreen path), return lx = floor((sx - cx - offX)/s), ly = floor((sy - cy)/s), where (cx,cy) = ClientToScreen(hwnd [0x6596CC], {0,0}), s = clientH/480 and offX = round((clientW - 640*s)/2). Leave out-of-range values to the game's own clamp.
Windowed path (flag 0): return cx + lx and cy + ly, so the game's own subtraction of the origin produces logical values.
Only one caller (0x42834A), so this covers the whole polled path: SGPMouseGetPos, IsCursorInRectangle, button repeats, KeyChange and the pick ray.
hook_points.serves_goal: (4) mouse mapping, screen to logical, for the polled position
hook_points.risks: Patch only the Wiz8.exe IAT slot, not user32 itself, so dgVoodoo and our own code still see real coordinates. Needs per-monitor DPI awareness, or every coordinate is DPI-virtualised. Rounding must match the SetCursorPos inverse or the cursor jitters.

hook_points.change:
Convert the incoming logical point back to screen: sx = cx + offX + ceil(lx*s), sy = cy + ceil(ly*s). In windowed mode subtract the client origin first.
Better: if the current real cursor already maps to the same (lx,ly), skip the warp. This keeps sub-logical-pixel motion smooth and avoids snapping.
Covers all six callers: 0x4280D6, 0x42812A, 0x4283CD, 0x42841B, 0x427B88, 0x427F92.
hook_points.serves_goal: (4) mouse mapping, logical to screen, for warps, clamping and hotspot changes
hook_points.risks: With s non-integer, a naive round() can map back to the neighbouring logical value. Use ceil, or skip the warp when it would be a no-op. Mouse-look warps to the centre (320,240) and measures deltas in logical units, so sensitivity drops by a factor of s (inferred, not measured).

hook_points.change:
In the detour, copy the MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT. If code >= 0 and msg is in 0x200..0x205, replace pt using the same screen-to-logical formula as the GetCursorPos hook. Fullscreen: logical value. Windowed: client origin + logical. Clamp to 0..639 x 0..479, or 0..640 x 0..480 to match the game. Then call the original with a pointer to the copy.
Optionally swallow button-downs in the pillarbox bars instead of clamping them onto the HUD edge.
This fixes the button and move event coordinates (event record +0xC) and the globals 0x6F050A/0x6F04F8 that game code reads directly.
Alternative with no inline patch: hook the IAT slot of SetWindowsHookExA at 0x005EB2B8 and, when idHook == 7, install a wrapper proc that transforms pt and forwards to 0x401C70.
hook_points.serves_goal: (4) mouse mapping for clicks: button events carry their own coordinates, independent of GetCursorPos
hook_points.risks: The original pass-through path calls CallNextHookEx with the lParam it received, so other hooks in the chain would see the modified copy (harmless; thread-local hook). The original has no clamp, so a negative value wraps through the 16-bit truncation to 0xFFxx. The clamp must therefore happen in our hook.

hook_points.change: Only if the 3D layer widens the projection while g_viewport stays in 4:3 logical units: scale Pick.x (float at +0, inferred) by aspect43/aspectReal before forwarding. That holds when the widened image's centre 4:3 region lines up with the 2D block and the vertical FOV is unchanged (Hor+). If g_viewport itself is widened instead, the logical cursor can never reach the side areas, and Pick.x must be computed from the real cursor.
hook_points.serves_goal: (3)/(4) 3D world picking stays correct under Hor+
hook_points.risks: Pick struct layout is inferred from the stack writes at 0x426B78-0x426BAC. pushPick may also be called from other sites (not enumerated). It depends on the camera and viewport approach chosen by the 3D subsystem.

hook_points.target: Confine the cursor to the 4:3 block (own ClipCursor, re-applied after the game's ClipCursor(NULL) at 0x402750, IAT slot 0x005EB230)
hook_points.change: While the game window is in the foreground, clip the OS cursor to the screen rect of the 4:3 block (cx+offX, cy, cx+offX+640*s, cy+480*s). Wrap the IAT ClipCursor so that the game's NULL becomes our block rect, and release the clip on deactivation.
hook_points.serves_goal: (4) polish: prevents the invisible OS cursor from drifting into the bars. SyncSystemCursor only warps when the logical value changes, so the cursor could otherwise go deep into a bar while the drawn cursor stays at the edge, creating a dead zone.
hook_points.risks: Must be released on Alt-Tab, focus loss and Bink playback. Conflicts with any wish to point into the widened 3D side areas.

hook_points.target: Alternative, not recommended: inline hooks on SyncSystemCursor 0x428340 and WarpSystemCursor 0x4280C0
hook_points.change: Reimplement SyncSystemCursor with scaling, and scale inside WarpSystemCursor.
hook_points.risks: Incomplete: SetMouseCursorHotspot 0x427F92 and SetMouseCursorFromVideoObject 0x427B88 call SetCursorPos directly with logical values, so the IAT approach is strictly better. Data-patching the 0x280/0x1E0 clamp constants (0x428363, 0x428370, 0x428381, 0x42838E, 0x428156, 0x428170) is also unnecessary.

Hook installation: bp 0x401F5F and check that the pushed args are 7 and 0x401C70; the handle lands in dd 0x6F050C.

Hotspot values: during play and when the cursor image changes, dump dd 0x6596BC L2 and set bp 0x427F00 / 0x427AB0. Confirm that position + hotspot stays invariant across the warps at 0x427F92 and 0x427B88.

Confirm the game takes the fullscreen path in our borderless setup: db 0x603C39 must be 01. If it is 00, the windowed branch is active and the hooks must add the client origin.

After installing the hooks: with s=2.25 (1080p), move the mouse 1 px at a time across the block and watch dd 0x654AD0. It must increase monotonically without jitter, and SetCursorPos calls should be skipped or idempotent. Click a known HUD button at its scaled screen position and at the bar edges.
Windowed /WINDOW in the original exe: resize the window larger than 640x480 and confirm that mouse mapping breaks (inferred: no scaling in either path).
open_questions: Does the borderless approach keep g_fullscreen (0x603C39) = 1, or run the windowed path? The hook formulas differ only by adding or removing the client origin, but the windowed path also toggles ShowCursor (0x6596C4) and tests the client rect in MouseHandler.

How is the OS cursor hidden in fullscreen? No ShowCursor(FALSE) appears on the fullscreen path of SyncSystemCursor; it is probably done elsewhere at init or by DirectDraw exclusive mode (not traced). In a borderless window the OS arrow may become visible on top of the drawn cursor.

Should clicks in the pillarbox bars be ignored, or clamped to the HUD edge? Should the cursor be able to point into the widened 3D side areas for picking? That would need logical x outside 0..640, which the clamps in 0x428340 and 0x428140 and the g_viewport-relative pick ray do not allow.
The exact layout of srGERD::Pick, and whether pushPick has other callers (only the RenderFrame site was examined).

The hotspot is added twice for repeat events (SGPMouseGetPos already includes it, and GetAtomCursorX adds it again). Is the hotspot normally 0? This needs a live check; it is not something the patch introduces.
DPI: is the process DPI-aware under dgVoodoo? If not, GetCursorPos, SetCursorPos and MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT.pt are DPI-virtualised, and s/offX must use the same coordinate space.
Mouse-look sensitivity becomes 1/s of the original, because deltas are measured in logical units after the warp to the centre (320,240). Is compensation needed? Inferred, not measured.

corrected_hook_points.change:
Call the real GetCursorPos to get (sx,sy). Let (cx,cy) = ClientToScreen(hwnd [0x6596CC], {0,0}), W/H = client size, offX = (W - (640*H)/480)/2. Use integer math with floor division (not C truncation): lx = floorDiv((sx-cx-offX)*480, H), ly = floorDiv((sy-cy)*480, H). If byte [0x603C39] != 0, return (lx,ly). Otherwise return (cx+lx, cy+ly), because the game subtracts the origin itself.
Optional anti-dead-zone: if lx/ly fall outside 0..640/0..480 and the game window is the foreground window, also move the real cursor to the nearest block edge with the real (unhooked) SetCursorPos. This removes the need for ClipCursor.

corrected_hook_points.risks: Truncating instead of flooring maps -0.5 to 0 and makes the left edge sticky. DPI virtualisation: make the process per-monitor DPI-aware (from our DLL, before the window is created) or compute every value in the same virtualised space. Our DLL and dgVoodoo must call the real API.

corrected_hook_points.change:
The incoming (x,y) is logical in fullscreen, or origin+logical in windowed mode (subtract the origin first). If the current real cursor already maps to the same (lx,ly) through the GetCursorPos formula, return TRUE without moving it. Otherwise sx = cx + offX + ceilDiv(lx*H, 480), sy = cy + ceilDiv(ly*H, 480), and call the real SetCursorPos. The round trip is exact: floor(ceil(L*s)/s) = L.
The skip rule is essential. SyncSystemCursor calls SetCursorPos on every logical change (0x4283CD), not only on clamps, so without the rule every frame would snap the cursor to the logical grid.
corrected_hook_points.serves_goal: (4) warps from all six sites (0x4280D6, 0x42812A, 0x4283CD, 0x42841B, 0x427B88, 0x427F92), including the clamp warp that pulls the cursor back from the bars
